runtime.execution: Tokio daemon/gRPC/UDS workers, SQLite records and managed external process-group drivers
runtime.service_boundary: owns workflow/scheduler/security/session/audit fabric; external CLI agents own providers and inner tool turns

summary: A substantial Rust workflow daemon manages native agent phases, parallel items, fenced terminal takeover and logical recovery. Its implemented self-build/exec mechanism is useful evidence, but drain and semantic-completion limits prevent a seamless-refit claim.

inspection.scope: Selected source excerpts trace exposed entry/loop/request/action/result/state boundaries and relevant capability mechanisms; listed tests are read as source only.
inspection.limits: No acquired code executed, dependencies installed or live providers invoked. Claims concern this pinned snapshot; untraced catalog tools and dependency internals are not inferred.

actions.name: orchestrator apply / Workflow resource
actions.input: YAML Agent/Workflow/StepTemplate/ExecutionProfile and related manifests; dry run/project
actions.lifecycle: validated config merge; live activation semantics vary by consumer
actions.authority: authorized daemon client; models may invoke CLI as external agents

actions.name: task create / start / pause / recover / retry / get
actions.input: goal, workflow, task/item ID, retry state
actions.lifecycle: scheduler owns queued/running status; bounded parallel item segments; pause kills process
actions.authority: daemon authorizes client; external agent may invoke orchestrator CLI

actions.name: shell/cli / claude/cli / codex/cli start
actions.input: prompt, model, session ref, timeout/profile, environment
actions.output: DriverSession event stream, PID and opaque session ref
actions.lifecycle: external child provider/tools; stream single consumer; semantic terminal can precede exit
actions.authority: configured driver/native tool policy and runner profile

actions.name: DriverSession.send / cancel
actions.input: user message/tool result/permission response or cancel
actions.lifecycle: Claude live input only; cancel returns before child reaping
actions.authority: driver host; native model processing receipt not exposed

actions.name: AgentSessionAttach / SendInput / read / detach / close
actions.input: session/client ID, lease/fencing token, 1–4096 input bytes and idempotency key
actions.lifecycle: writer lease and process identity; accepted means FIFO write, not model read

actions.name: run_tests
actions.output: exit code and stdout/stderr evidence paths
actions.lifecycle: awaited allowlisted test child with deadline/capture
actions.authority: authenticated run token and allowed tool set; governed runner profile

actions.name: mark_item / mark_done / generate_items / record_metric
actions.input: status+summary; bounded item IDs/vars/replace; bounded numeric name/value
actions.output: updated item status, generated count, metric record

actions.name: create_ticket / scan_tickets
actions.output: deduplicated ticket path or active ticket list
actions.lifecycle: requires failing evidence; tracks QA issue outside immediate repair
actions.authority: authenticated allowed run; narrower than free-form rageshake

actions.name: handoff.generate / resume.plan / resume.execute
actions.input: task/boundary/mode, actor, state version and approval context
actions.output: immutable snapshot, expiring consequence plan, correlated logical resume
actions.authority: authorized controller with elevated confirmation for replay-risk class

actions.name: self_test / self_restart builtin
actions.lifecycle: build then deferred task drain and same-PID daemon exec; drain failures do not all fence exec
actions.authority: workflow author selects builtin; mechanism supports modifying own harness

actions.name: task timeline / trace / logs
actions.output: sanitized persisted event/run projections and output
actions.lifecycle: cursor-based projection; retention may prune terminal events
actions.authority: authorized read client; native provider internals not fully captured

filesystem.detail: Runner external shell/native-agent processes act on configured workspace; compiler/test/file output paths exposed. Inner native editor/tool implementation belongs to separate agents.

processes.detail: Rust daemon spawns managed process groups with profiles/environment policy and sanitized streams; cancellation owns group kill, but API result/cancel is not necessarily reaped completion.

code_actions.detail: Workflow shell commands, CRD command hooks and external model agent tools can execute authored programs; orchestrator itself supplies named coordination tools rather than code kernel.

persistent_kernel.detail: Control plane launches/manages external agent/command processes; no native computation notebook/kernel role in inspected driver/workflow path.

standing_database.detail: Embedded SQLite stores task/event/config/session state and queries; model coordination tools expose narrow task data, not arbitrary standing database computation.

workflow_programming.detail: YAML step/loop/capability resources, prompt templates and bounded parallel item segments run external agents; model tools generate task items and metrics. Separate DAG struct is not assumed to be live scheduler.

multi_model.detail: Different native/shell drivers and per-driver model arguments allow heterogeneous workflow phases/parallel items.

live_collaboration.detail: Run-scoped tools manipulate shared task/item evidence and delegated workflow work; interactive FIFO steering exists. No peer room/mail/chat transport established in these traced tools/drivers.

concurrent_work.detail: Daemon workers and semaphore-bounded JoinSet execute task/items; collect-all segment errors and per-item state.

steering_interrupt.detail: Task pause kills active children; terminal takeover uses fenced input lease. Driver cancel only signals background task and scheduler returns without reaped/captured end.

turn_redefinition.detail: Model provider turn lives in external CLI; manifests choose workflow phases/templates and model coordination tools, not inner per-request turn program.

compaction.detail: No managed native context-compaction policy established in selected control-plane/driver/session/handoff trace; provider owns inner transcript.

context_repair.detail: Logical handoff/resume plans project persisted task state with explicit replay consequence and optional provider-session reuse; not editable authoritative provider context repair.

original_audit.detail: Task/control/session records and sanitized stdout exist, but coordination logging can fail silently and omits arguments/results; streams redact originals and retention prunes events.

audit_query.detail: Task timeline cursor and trace join persisted command runs/events with redaction/anomaly projections; coverage remains recorded control-plane scope.

hot_change.detail: Manifest config apply changes persisted resources; current phase/parallel segment retain captured request/task context. Uniform affected-turn/workflow activation policy not established across resource consumers.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Real self-build/verification/hash/pending-state→deferred other-task drain→same-PID exec is implemented. Native terminal events may precede OS exit, drain timeout does not block exec, and no outpost/session transport transfer.

remote_services.detail: gRPC/UDS client consumes daemon-owned scheduler/SQLite/security fabric; model providers are external native CLIs. Suitable as external-fabric reference, not Arconaut consumer core.

self_improvement.detail: Workflow can run own implement/test/rebuild cycles, model tools record metrics/generate work and create QA tickets. Build --help/snapshot do not establish model-governed experiment validity or safe executable refit.

complaints.detail: create_ticket records deduplicated QA failure linked to stdout/stderr after run_tests; no unrestricted frustration/state snapshot complaint action in traced catalog.

authority.detail: Runner profiles/environment allowlist and self-PID guard; native permission mapping and callback token/run allowlist; terminal writer lease/fencing/idempotency. Configurable governed control-plane orientation differs from unrestricted operator intent.

evaluation.detail: Read real-child driver signal/exit tests distinguish OS kill from ordinary failure; restart readiness test uses fake cargo/fake help binary and asserts SQLite/stable file, not actual exec/session/drain continuity.

time_order.detail: Persisted task/event cursors and fenced idempotent FIFO reservation improve control ordering; provider semantic Finished before capture/exit and write-before-audit external effect prevent completion/quiescence equivalence.

evidence.claim: Control plane wraps external shell/native coding agents through gRPC/UDS daemon, workers and embedded SQLite; not an inner model tool loop.
YAML workflow resource validates steps/loop constraints and applies a resource representation; custom nonempty step IDs resolve as agent capabilities.

Manifest apply parses/validates and merges current SQLite-backed config; invalid documents accumulate errors while valid documents are processed. Exact activation for every runtime policy is outside this trace.
Phase run carries task/item/step/provider/session/execution-profile context and enters setup, then spawn/wait/validation/record stages.
TTY phase may return early; ordinary phase waits driver result, drops coordination tool host, validates selected driver/output events and remembers native session reference.
Item segments spawn bounded JoinSet with semaphore, optional stagger and per-item finalization; collects all results, errors and completeness count.
Shell, Claude and Codex drivers launch external commands and ProcessSession; Claude takes structured input, shell closes initial stdin, Codex command owns prompt.
Native driver maps model/budget/turn/permission options and opaque resume references; Claude allows run-scoped MCP callback tools, raw args pass through.
Runner enforces profile/policy, creates process group, kill-on-drop, environment allowlist and self-daemon-kill guard before child spawn.
Explicit Unix cancellation SIGKILLs child process group; non-Unix falls back to direct child kill.

ProcessSession owns separate stdout/stderr capture and background wait task; cancellation triggers group kill and reaping; events are unbounded, native terminal event suppresses later process-status terminal.
Driver events consumed once; send writes/flushed stdin and only Claude accepts live input encoding; cancel merely signals background oneshot and returns.
Parsed provider events are emitted before sanitized line write; terminal flag can be set before process exit/output capture completes. Session identifiers are redacted in saved output.
Claude protocol result becomes Finished with semantic success/error and no OS signal, rather than a reaped-process observation.
Scheduler treats Finished as end of phase; timeout/stall/pause calls cancel then returns without waiting for OS exit/capture reaping. Heartbeat uses output byte changes.
Task pause sets stop flag, kills current/DB child then updates task state and inserts task_control; not cooperative standing-service suspension.
Authenticated loopback run tools enforce per-run allowed set, execute effects and return structured result; started/completed event insertion errors are ignored, payloads omit tool arguments/results.
run_tests maps allowlisted target to command, persists sanitized output, applies timeout and waits capture on normal exit.
create_ticket requires last failing run_tests evidence; scan_tickets queries current item; generate_items validates bounded IDs then creates dynamic items and records event.
Exact model catalog is run_tests, mark_item, mark_done, create_ticket, scan_tickets, generate_items and record_metric, filtered to run allowlist.
stdio MCP shim forwards JSON-RPC to bearer-authenticated daemon callback; effects remain in daemon, shim owns no collaboration state.
Interactive input requires byte limit, idempotency key, process identity and valid writer fencing token; audit reservation distinguishes accepted/in-progress/hash conflict.
Accepted input means atomic FIFO write followed by database outcome, not model consumption; crash between external FIFO and outcome remains distinct boundary.
Resume plan persists expiring logical boundary with state fingerprint, effect class and consequences; explicitly no workspace rollback and provider resume fallback.
Self-restart performs actual cargo build then new binary --help with timeout, rejects failed build/verification.
Build hashes old/new binaries, snapshots new stable file, sets restart_pending and persists self_restart_ready event before signaling exec readiness.
Self-restart defers while other registered tasks remain; completion unregisters and can trigger shutdown when running registry reaches zero.
Daemon shutdown signals workers, gives five seconds then forces task kill; interactive session drain is separate best-effort reclaim.
Supervisor drain timeout/panic and pending-reset error log but do not prevent exec of new daemon with same PID/args. No outpost chat transfer.
Capture redacts stream before file write and flushes; no raw retention/fsync proof.
Timeline queries persisted source with cursor watermark and redaction patterns.
Trace joins recorded events and command runs for timeline/anomaly projection.
Retention deletes old terminal-task events in bounded batches; event database is not indefinite complete audit.

tests.focus: Real child stdin and OS signal versus ordinary exit propagation
tests.oracle: cat child exact output and kill-XCPU/exit-3 assertions challenge process→DriverEvent boundary; unexecuted source, not live providers.

tests.focus: Self-restart readiness and persisted pending state
tests.oracle: Fake cargo exits zero and fake new binary serves help; asserts RestartReady, SQLite restart_pending and stable file. Does not perform real compiler/exec or prove concurrent worker quiescence.

strengths: Typed driver events and real OS signal boundary tests.
Logical resume consequences explicitly distinguish replay from workspace rollback.
limits: Native protocol Finished can precede output persistence and process reaping; scheduler exits that boundary early.
Cancel signals without await, and daemon supervisor drain timeout logs then exec continues.
Sanitized control-plane logs are selective/retained, coordination audit failures ignored.
Shared daemon owns orchestration fabric; peer live room and inner model loop belong elsewhere.
arconaut_questions: What exact barrier makes no active provider/processes a precondition for binary switch?
Can rebuild supervision transfer to an independent outpost while this daemon remains consumer-only?
Should semantic answer, process exit, output persisted and effects committed be separate lifecycle events?
